bias_targets.methodology: Projecting image embeddings of 301 historical and modern artworks onto a bipolar semantic axis ('apolitical neutral' to 'political engaged') to measure and compare how different vision-language models implicitly attribute political categorization to visual data.

Evaluating algorithmic coloniality and ethnocentric bias by analyzing how models differentially categorize Western versus non-Western art (e.g., African masks) using semantic axes such as 'aesthetic/formal' versus 'colonial/exoticism'.

Measuring models' differential sensitivity to visual properties and object representation by projecting image embeddings onto axes such as 'building-landscape' versus 'human body-face' and 'ideal body' versus 'violence/trauma' to detect corporeal realism biases.
